title: Cleaner Air Could Prevent or Postpone 9.4 Million Deaths a Year
title_zh: 剑桥研究：达到世卫空气质量标准，一年或可避免或推迟940万例死亡
source_name: University of Cambridge — “Over 9 million lives could be saved every year if countries met WHO air quality guidelines” (10 Nov 2026)
summary_zh: 剑桥大学研究人员11月10日在《环境国际》发表研究指出，若136个低收入和中等收入国家达到世界卫生组织对细颗粒物（PM 2.5）的年均指导标准，一年内估计可避免或推迟940万例死亡；若达到二氧化氮标准，则约为110万例，二者不宜简单相加。即便只达到较为宽松的过渡目标，与PM 2.5相关的死亡仍可能减少约660万例。更清洁的空气还可减少冠心病、中风、慢性阻塞性肺病和失智症的新发病例，并降低直接医疗费用、提高劳动生产率。研究者强调，交通、城市规划和能源方面的决策可以改善空气，经济发展不必以牺牲公众健康为代价。
paragraphs: Researchers at the University of Cambridge say that meeting World Health Organization guidelines for two air pollutants could prevent or postpone more than nine million deaths in one year in low- and middle-income countries. The 10 November study in Environment International also looks at healthcare costs and preventable illness.

Outdoor air pollution is the largest environmental threat to human health. It has been linked to coronary heart disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD, and dementia. In 2021, the WHO tightened annual limits for fine particulate matter, known as PM 2.5, and for nitrogen dioxide. PM 2.5 can be breathed deep into the lungs and comes from vehicle emissions, power plants and construction dust. Nitrogen dioxide is mainly produced when fossil fuels are burned.

The problem is serious in low- and middle-income countries, where air quality has often worsened alongside large-scale urbanisation. The Cambridge team studied 136 of these countries, using computer models to estimate what would happen if pollution fell to the WHO's recommended levels or to less strict interim targets.

Reaching the WHO guideline for PM 2.5 could prevent or postpone an estimated 9.4 million deaths in one year. Meeting the guideline for nitrogen dioxide could prevent or postpone around 1.1 million deaths. Less strict interim targets would bring substantial benefits: about 6.6 million fewer deaths linked to PM 2.5 and 435,000 linked to nitrogen dioxide.

Meeting the recommended PM 2.5 levels could mean fewer new cases of disease: 2.8 million for COPD, 1.1 million for dementia, 7.3 million for coronary heart disease and 2.3 million for stroke. Direct medical costs could fall by 11.8 billion dollars for coronary heart disease, 5.9 billion for stroke and 8.6 billion for dementia. Productivity gains could reach 18.1 billion, 17.9 billion and 5.3 billion dollars for COPD, stroke and coronary heart disease.

Cambridge researcher Dr Annalan Navaratnam said the team had modelled the potential benefits of the WHO's clean air guidelines in the most polluted countries. Dr Haneen Khreis warned that meeting the guideline values will not be straightforward, but said these countries have a critical opportunity as their cities expand. Decisions about transport, urban planning and energy can change the air people breathe, she said, and economic development need not come at the expense of public health.
paragraphs_zh: 剑桥大学的研究人员表示，若达到世界卫生组织针对两种常见空气污染物的指导标准，低收入和中等收入国家在一年内或可避免或推迟900多万例死亡。这项11月10日发表在《环境国际》（Environment International）上的研究，还考察了医疗成本以及可预防疾病造成的影响。
室外空气污染是对人类健康威胁最大的环境因素。它与冠心病、中风、慢性阻塞性肺病（COPD）以及失智症有关。2021年，世界卫生组织收紧了细颗粒物（即PM 2.5）和二氧化氮的年均上限。PM 2.5可以被吸入肺部深处，来自汽车尾气、发电厂和建筑扬尘。二氧化氮主要在化石燃料燃烧时产生。
这一问题在低收入和中等收入国家较为严重：随着大规模城市化，这些国家的空气质量往往已经恶化。剑桥大学的研究团队考察了其中136个国家，并利用计算机模型估算：如果污染降至世卫组织建议的水平，或降至较为宽松的过渡目标，情况会如何变化。
若达到世卫组织的PM 2.5指导标准，一年内估计可避免或推迟940万例死亡。若达到二氧化氮的指导标准，则或可避免或推迟约110万例死亡。较为宽松的过渡目标仍会带来显著益处：与PM 2.5相关的死亡约减少660万例，与二氧化氮相关的死亡约减少43.5万例。
达到建议的PM 2.5水平，还可能减少疾病新发病例：慢性阻塞性肺病280万例、失智症110万例、冠心病730万例、中风230万例。冠心病、中风和失智症的直接医疗费用或可分别下降118亿、59亿和86亿美元。生产率收益在慢性阻塞性肺病、中风和冠心病方面或可分别达到181亿、179亿和53亿美元。
剑桥大学研究员安纳兰·纳瓦拉特南博士表示，研究团队已模拟出世卫组织清洁空气指导标准在污染最严重国家可能带来的益处。哈宁·赫雷斯博士警告说，达到这些指导值并不容易，但她认为，随着城市扩张，这些国家仍有一个关键机会。她说，交通、城市规划和能源方面的决策可以改变人们呼吸的空气，而经济发展不必以牺牲公众健康为代价。

室外空气污染；户外空气污染

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Diesel vehicles are the only source of outdoor air pollution in wealthy countries.
A Cambridge study finds that meeting WHO air quality guidelines in 136 low- and middle-income countries could prevent or postpone millions of deaths and also cut medical costs.
The World Health Organization will ban all fossil fuels in 2021.
Air pollution has already been eliminated in every city that the researchers studied.
questions.explanation: 主旨：剑桥大学的研究表明，若136个中低收入国家达到世卫组织空气质量指导标准，一年内或可避免或推迟数百万人死亡，并降低医疗费用。

evidence.quote: meeting World Health Organization guidelines for two air pollutants could prevent or postpone more than nine million deaths in one year in low- and middle-income countries

questions.prompt: According to the study, how many deaths could be prevented or postponed in one year if countries met the WHO guideline for PM 2.5?
questions.explanation: 第4段写明：达到世卫组织的PM 2.5指导标准，一年内估计可避免或推迟940万例死亡。约110万是二氧化氮标准的估计，43.5万是过渡目标下与二氧化氮相关的减少数，118亿则是冠心病直接医疗费用的美元数字。

evidence.quote: Reaching the WHO guideline for PM 2.5 could prevent or postpone an estimated 9.4 million deaths in one year.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from Dr Haneen Khreis's comments?
options: Poor countries must stop all economic growth in order to clean their air.
Only new medical technology, not transport or energy policy, can reduce air pollution.
Growth and cleaner air can go together if governments make better choices about transport, cities and energy.
Meeting the WHO targets will be easy for every country this year.
questions.explanation: 赫雷斯指出，交通、城市规划和能源方面的决策可以改变人们呼吸的空气，而且经济发展不必以牺牲公众健康为代价。由此可推断：如果政府在交通、城市和能源上做出更好的选择，增长与更清洁的空气可以并行。

evidence.quote: Decisions about transport, urban planning and energy can change the air people breathe, she said, and economic development need not come at the expense of public health.
